title: Anticipatory prefetch SDK surface and compact stream PRD
body:
Summary
This PRD sketch proposes a lightweight SDK surface and server-side runtime behavior we call 'anticipatory prefetch' (APF) for the Hosted API. APF is a coordinated client+server pattern that aims to reduce tail latency for common tool-calling and progressive structured-output scenarios without increasing token cost materially.

Motivation / problem statement
- Observed problem: latencies for the first substantive structured-frame (e.g., tool call result, JSON block) vary widely due to model tokenization pacing, network RTT, and cold cache on the server (KV cache + kernel selection). App owners want predictable end-to-end 95th percentile latency for tool-dependent flows (search calls, DB lookups, HTTP fetches).
- Current tradeoffs: increasing server-side batching improves throughput but raises end-to-end latency and jitter. Clients implementing aggressive local prefetch/batching end up complex and brittle in mobile/edge networks.
- Opportunity: expose a minimal SDK surface that codifies a few opt-in heuristics and signals so the runtime can safely speculatively prepare variants of the model execution path (shorter quantized variants, warmed prefix-KV caches, pre-allocated tool adapters) and the client can reduce perceived latency via progressive frames.

Goals (success metrics)
- Primary: reduce median-to-95th latency for tool-first responses by 20–40% across typical e2e stacks for Customers A/B tested.
- Secondary: keep incremental token cost delta under 5% (no significant budget drift).
- Operational: enable per-route telemetry for speculative events and allow opt-out per-customer or per-route.
- Developer ergonomics: provide an SDK that requires <5 lines to opt into APF per route and has clear fallbacks.

Non-goals
- This is not a replacement for full canary/rollout infra. APF should be opt-in and reversible.
- Not intended to change user-visible model semantics (no hallucination-improving strategies here).

High-level design
- Concept: client sends a lightweight intent/affordance hint alongside the regular streaming request. The hint indicates the expected shape of the next action (e.g., tool_call:search(query), structured_frame:inventory-json). The server treats this hint as speculative guidance to prepare execution paths and optionally return a compact early frame if available.
- Two key capabilities: 1) prefetching of model artifacts and runtime buffers; 2) compact progressive frames allowing earliest useful data to reach the app.

SDK ergonomics (surface proposal)
- Minimal opt-in call: specify prefetch hints in request metadata. Example minimal pseudo-call: 
  createStream({
    model: 'rw-7b-infer',
    prefetch: {
      hint: 'tool_call:search',
      priority: 'low'
    }
  })
- High-level APIs:
  - prefetchHint: string (freeform but recommended canonical values shipped in SDK: tool_call:search, tool_call:lookup, structured:json, structured:yaml, speculative:summary)
  - prefetchPriority: enum (low, normal, high) - controls server resource hedging
  - prefetchBudget: integer (optional token-equivalent ceiling to avoid runaway cost)
  - onEarlyFrame(callback) - callback for progressive frames (partial JSON, status)
- Default behavior: SDK will not prefetch unless explicit hint present. SDK includes a small convenience helper to infer hints from prompt templates (e.g., detect 'SEARCH:' block).

Server-side runtime behavior (how APF will be handled)
- Priority allocation: prefetchPriority maps to a small QoS bucket; high may trigger hot-path with warmed KV caches / prefer low-latency kernel selection, low maps to background preparation.
- Speculative kernel selection: for certain model types the runtime can create a short-latency variant execution (e.g., lower-precision micro-batch) to produce an initial structured frame while the full-precision generation continues.
- Early compact frames: if the runtime can determine a partial structured artifact (e.g., extracted JSON keys), it will emit a compact frame: {frame_type: 'compact_struct', payload: base64-compressed-json} as part of the normal incremental stream. Clients receive this as onEarlyFrame.
- Cost accounting: speculative actions are tracked and billed under an 'anticipatory' ledger so tenants can inspect/disable per-route. Speculative work is only applied to a small percentage of tokens per request as controlled by prefetchBudget/default limits.

Structured output contract
- Payloads: we propose a small versioned envelope for compact frames: version, kind, minimal schema path, sample_hash. This helps clients validate whether the compact frame is sufficient or they need to wait for full stream.
- Schema negotiation: clients may attach an optional 'schema_hint' string (JSONPath or small spec) to say what shape they prefer. Server will avoid early-frame emission if it cannot meet the schema hint.
- Reconciliation: every compact frame includes a content-hash and an eventual canonical frame in the final stream will include the same hash when applicable. If the final result differs, client receives a corrected frame and an event with reason: conflict/rescoped/expanded.

Tool-calling flow and edge cases
- Typical flow: model produces tool_call intent -> SDK prefetch hint activated -> runtime warms adapter -> model emits tool_call frame quickly -> client receives compact tool response or a tool-invocation token and executes the tool -> tool result integrated into final stream.
- Race conditions: when both client and server can call tools, SDK provides a deterministic tie-breaker: server-first (default) or client-first (opt-in) based on route config.
- Security: speculative prefetch never executes external network calls. It only prepares the environment and possible parameterization. Actual tool invocation must still be an explicit, authenticated action from the runtime once the model output asks for it.

Telemetry and observability
- Events to emit: prefetch_requested, prefetch_started, prefetch_warmed, early_frame_emitted, early_frame_reconciled, speculative_cost_charged. Each event includes route, prefetch_hint, prefetch_priority, and latency buckets.
- Console UX: add a per-route toggle to show APF % of requests, average speculative tokens, and delta to median P95.

Backward compatibility and migration strategy
- Opt-in first: keep default off. Roll out to internal beta customers and Redwood-provided SDK sample apps.
- Gradual expansion: start with two stable hints (tool_call:search and structured:json) and the 'normal' priority. Expand hints after telemetry validates cost/benefit.
- Safety net: ability to set global or org-level kill-switch; route override to disable APF for sensitive workloads.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should speculative kernel selection be? (Perf teams to provide measured throughput/accuracy tradeoff for candidate models).
- What's an acceptable prefetchBudget default that reduces tail latency but doesn't open cost surprises?
- Should the runtime surface a richer serialization format than base64-compressed-json for ultra-low-bandwidth clients?
- How to ensure compact frames do not inadvertently leak partial PII when model emits fragments? (Security review required.)

Implementation milestones (rough)
- Phase 0 (2–4 weeks): SDK shape PR + server gating flags + telemetry stubs. Internal prototype with rw-7b on dev cluster.
- Phase 1 (6–8 weeks): runtime speculative warm paths, compact frame envelope, internal load test. Gather cost and latency matrices.
- Phase 2 (4–6 weeks): beta release to 3 customers, console telemetry, kill-switch, and initial docs.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): iterate hints, extend to more models, and refine default priorities.

Appendix: example developer patterns and recommended defaults
- Mobile-first (default): prefetchPriority: low, prefetchBudget: 20 tokens-equivalent, schema_hint: 'top-level-objects'
- High-latency server-side apps: prefetchPriority: normal, prefetchBudget: 60
- Real-time search assistant: prefetchPriority: high, prefetchHint: 'tool_call:search'

Notes / references
- Related tickets: JIRA HOSTED-1742 (tooling prefetch spike analysis), HOSTED-1801 (stream frame envelope).
- Slack thread: #hosted-api-tooling-thread-oz5 has early UX sketches and mobile customer asks.

Next steps
- Product: validate the two canonical hints and agree on prefetchBudget defaults.
- Engineering: prototype SDK integration and runtime gating with telemetry.
- Security: schedule threat model review focused on compact frames and partial output leakage.

Comments welcome — adding rough estimation numbers and perf comparison tables will be done in follow-up doc.
